daily_brief: G7 foreign ministers convened in Paris on Monday with Secretary of State Marco Rubio facing pressure from European allies over the Iran war and Ukraine negotiations, days after Republicans suffered major midterm losses widely attributed to the unpopularity of the conflict [RFI, France 24, Le Monde]. The meeting precedes US-Russia-Ukraine talks scheduled for Tuesday in Abu Dhabi. In Poland, the suspect in Saturday's Krakow mass shooting that killed nine people—including six in the city center and three family members—died in hospital, as authorities continued investigating potential far-right motivations while politicians debated the gunman's ideology [BBC, ABC Australia]. COP31 opened in Antalya, Turkey, with US delegates attending but not participating in negotiations, as nations remain divided over fossil fuel commitments and climate finance for developing countries [RFI]. In South Africa, local election results showed the ANC falling to under 32% of the national vote, marking a historic decline for the party that has governed since 1994 [The Guardian]. Meanwhile, at least 13 migrants drowned off the coast of Crete as Mediterranean crossings continue to surge past 2025 levels [BBC, Le Monde].

top_stories.headline: G7 Ministers Press Rubio on Iran War and Ukraine as US Faces Post-Midterm Diplomatic Reckoning
bullets: G7 foreign ministers met in Paris on Monday, with Ukraine and Iran topping the agenda ahead of US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday
Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the Iran war as necessary to prevent nuclear proliferation, despite its role in Republican midterm losses
Democrats won control of both houses of Congress in last week's midterms, widely seen as a rebuke of Trump's foreign policy
France's Foreign Minister Barrot confirmed European participation in the Abu Dhabi talks, with discussions potentially moving toward a multilateral format

sources.framing_note: Focused on European perspective and coalition dynamics

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Iran's view of midterms as 'golden opportunity' for negotiations

sources.framing_note: Highlighted Rubio's defense of war as 'not necessarily popular but needed'

top_stories.headline: Krakow Mass Shooting Suspect Dies as Poland Debates Gunman's Far-Right Links
bullets: The 24-year-old Polish gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square and three family members at his home died in hospital on Monday
Two police officers who engaged the shooter within three minutes and prevented further casualties emerged from comas on Sunday
Authorities initially cited far-right ideology as a possible motive but have since said the investigation remains ongoing
A British national and Austrian woman were among the six killed in the public attack; 15 others were wounded

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed timeline and highlighted heroic actions of surgeons and police

sources.name: ABC Australia
sources.framing_note: Emphasized political dispute over motive claims, noting opposition accused government of lying

top_stories.headline: COP31 Opens in Turkey with US Observers Only as Nations Remain Divided on Fossil Fuels
bullets: UN climate talks began Monday in Antalya, Turkey, running until November 20 under a joint Turkish-Australian arrangement
US delegates will attend but not participate in negotiations, following the Trump administration's climate policy shifts
UNEP warned in October that existing policies could drive warming to 2.8°C this century, with a sustained breach of 1.5°C now considered unavoidable
Poorer nations are pressing for climate finance to address floods and droughts while fossil fuel commitments remain contentious

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Detailed the overshoot scenario and UN warnings about current trajectory

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Focused on electrification as a key theme amid extreme weather events

top_stories.headline: ANC Falls Below 32% in South African Local Elections, Marking Historic Decline
bullets: The ANC received 31.8% of the national vote with over 80% of ballots counted, down nearly 14 points from 2021
The party is projected to lose its position as the largest party in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa's two most populous provinces
The Democratic Alliance received 24.1% and Jacob Zuma's MK party received 9.3%
Voter turnout increased to approximately 54.5%, up from 46% in the previous local elections

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Framed results as continuation of ANC decline since end of apartheid, citing unemployment, crime, and corruption as factors

top_stories.headline: At Least 13 Migrants Drown Off Crete as Mediterranean Crossings Surge
bullets: Thirteen Sudanese nationals died when their boat sank approximately 15 nautical miles off the coast of Crete
Eighteen survivors were rescued, with four including a toddler taken to hospital
Authorities believe the boat had been at sea for days and struggled to reach shore due to strong winds
More than 37,000 migrants have arrived in Greece in 2026, already surpassing the 2025 total, with over 22,000 landing in Crete alone

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed casualty figures and context on Greek migration patterns

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Reported higher death toll of 20 migrants
